input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
input.rationale: Section 17(b) gives Sparkling an unconditional right to terminate the Agreement at any time on ninety (90) calendar days' written notice, which sits squarely in the fallback range of 60–90 days, and no early-termination fee, penalty or forfeiture is imposed anywhere in the Agreement (Sections 11 and 17 impose none), so the fallback three-month fee cap is exceeded in our favour. Garman has no convenience termination right at all: Section 17(a) makes the licence perpetual so long as fees are paid, and Garman's only exit routes are the mutual insolvency/material-default triggers in Section 17(c); the Section 10 maintenance term is expressly "renewable" with no Garman discontinuation right. That is better than the fallback (Vendor end-of-term convenience on 90 days' notice) and satisfies the preferred element that Vendor have no mid-term convenience right. Short of preferred only in that our notice period is 90 rather than 30 days and there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on a 17(b) termination (a refund of fees for services not rendered applies only on termination for Garman's default under Section 17(c)); these are minor sub-elements noted rather than redlined. The clause therefore sits at (and in part above) the fallback and we do not propose changes.
